records.claim: Formal objections to Arizona and Pennsylvania electoral votes were raised during Congress's January 6–7, 2021 count; neither objection was sustained by either chamber.
records.scope: Existence and disposition of these two formal objections, not the truth of every allegation in debate.
records.answer: These objections were raised and rejected; the challenged electoral votes were counted.
records.author: @adrian.factomaton
records.change_summary: Replace the NARA relative paragraph locator with an opening-text anchor and sentence-order description after different-owner review. This revision addresses locator precision.

prior_review.carryover: Historical v2 acceptance. V3 requires fresh exact-version review.

evidence.locator: Notes, passage beginning During the electoral vote count, objections were filed with respect to the Arizona and Pennsylvania electoral votes, before the certification-time sentence and the Electoral College Certificates and Votes by State heading
evidence.observation: Records both objections, their rejection by both chambers, and counting of all electoral votes.

evidence.edition: Corrected online Congressional Record, Volume 167 Number 4, House H76–H115
evidence.locator: H77 Arizona written objection; H98 Pennsylvania written objection and H99 Perry debate; H94 Arizona rejection orders at resumed 11:35 p.m. joint session; H113 Pennsylvania rejection orders at resumed 3:22 a.m. joint session
evidence.observation: Records formal objections and both chambers' rejection orders, followed by counting each original certificate. Debate records allegations, not proof.

limitations: Preserving an objection is not endorsing its allegations.
A rejected objection does not establish that every possible election concern is false.
Both sources concern the same congressional count; they are not independent audits.
Author and reviewer share Adrian as owner; internal review is not independent community confirmation.
